question: As of February 2025, Scheduled Tribe (ST) individuals comprising ____ of the total population in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.086**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes (ST) Population in India:** As of **February 2025**, individuals from Scheduled Tribes (ST) constitute about **8.6% (0.086)** of India’s total population. This figure is derived from the latest population data and census reports. 
 
• **Census Data:** The **Census of India 2011** reported that Scheduled Tribes made up **8.6%** of the total population. Projections for 2025 have maintained this percentage, considering demographic trends. 
 
• **Geographical Concentration:** Scheduled Tribes primarily reside in regions such as **Northeast India, central India, and parts of southern and western India**. States like **Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan** have significant ST populations. 
 
• **Constitutional Recognition:** Scheduled Tribes are recognized under **Article 342** of the Indian Constitution. This recognition enables the government to provide these communities with special protections and development schemes. 
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Various programs, such as the **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana**, have been implemented to improve the socio-economic conditions of Scheduled Tribes, focusing on education, healthcare, and employment generation. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes Definition:** Scheduled Tribes are identified as communities that are **socially and economically disadvantaged**. They have unique cultural and social practices that distinguish them from the broader population. 
 
• **Demographic Distribution:** According to the **Census 2011**, the total number of Scheduled Tribes in India was approximately **10.45 crore**. The population growth rate among STs has been consistent with national averages. 
 
• **Major ST Communities:** Prominent Scheduled Tribes include the **Santhals, Bhils, Gonds, Oraons, Nagas, Mizos, and Khasi**. Each community has its own distinct language, customs, and traditions. 
 
• **Tribal Areas:** Specific regions, known as **“Scheduled Areas”**, have been designated under the Indian Constitution to safeguard the rights and autonomy of Scheduled Tribes. These areas are governed under **Fifth and Sixth Schedules**. 
 
• **Legislative Framework:** The Indian government has enacted laws such as the **Forest Rights Act (2006)** and the **Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 1996** to protect the land and cultural rights of Scheduled Tribes. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Educational Initiatives:** The Indian government has introduced programs like the **Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme** and the establishment of **Eklavya Model Residential Schools** to improve literacy and education among ST communities. 
 
• **Economic Development:** Livelihood initiatives such as the **Van Dhan Vikas Kendra** aim to enhance the income of tribal communities through the sustainable use of forest resources. 
 
• **Health Disparities:** Despite progress, Scheduled Tribes face challenges in accessing healthcare. Government schemes like **Ayushman Bharat** and targeted tribal health programs aim to bridge these gaps. 
 
• **Political Representation:** Reserved seats in **Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies** ensure political representation for Scheduled Tribes, empowering them to voice their concerns in governance.
